The project title is "Filecoin virtual machine".
Data DAOs are decentralized autonomous organizations whose ownership, governance, and decision-making processes are transparently conducted via on-chain activities.
Data DAOs have a mission focused on preservation, curation, augmentation, and promotion of high-value datasets.
Examples of Data DAO datasets include large genomic or research databases, historical indexed blockchain chain and transaction data, rollup data, the Wikipedia, NFT collections, and metaverse assets.
Stake in Data DAOs can be tokenized so the value and utility of data can be expressed and transacted in markets.
Interested parties could harvest tokens by analyzing datasets, performing scientific and ML modelling, and calculating statistics.
Stakeholders could spend tokens to incentivize more production of raw data such as sensor data collection, generative art, and human tasks like transcription and translation.
The Filecoin virtual machine can implement ingredients to make Data DAOs a reality by creating composable layers that can be combined to form different kinds of DAOs.
Perpetual storage is described as a Filecoin virtual machine use case.
Many common-good datasets rely on stewarding organizations to ensure preservation and continued accessibility.
Examples of common-good datasets include crime statistics, inflation metrics, election results, and environmental data records.
When responsibility for common-good data lies on a single organization, it can create a central point of failure and trust.
If the stewarding organization goes away or changes motivation, common-good data could be lost forever or manipulated.
With Filecoin actors, responsibility for ensuring liveness of valuable data can be shared collectively.
Permissionless code running autonomously on-chain can guarantee continuation and renewal of storage.
Content-addressing is described as preventing risk of modification or alteration of underlying datasets.
Funding mechanisms and decision-making can be coupled with Data DAOs and Staking Protocols to enable pay-once-store-forever mechanics.
